references.text: Peter refers directly to Balaam's donkey, which spoke with a human voice and prevented the prophet from going astray. This is the clearest New Testament reference to the event in Numbers 22:28.
The serpent spoke to Eve in the Garden of Eden. This is another example in Scripture where an animal speaks, although the circumstances are different.
The Lord also opened Balaam's eyes so that he could see the angel. This shows that God can open both mouths and eyes to reveal His will.
The angel confirms that the donkey had seen him and turned aside three times, which explains why the donkey acted as it did.
The Lord asks Moses who has given man a mouth and promises to be with his mouth. This shows that God has power over speech and can give the ability to speak to whomever He chooses.
